source: Classic Traveller Book 3: Worlds and Adventures, Second Edition (GDW)

definitions.name: Herbivores
definitions.definition: Animals which eat unresisting food are generally classed as herbivores. While this is usually construed as covering plant eaters, the definition is extended here to cover the eating of unresisting animals as well. For example, the anteater and the whale eat effectively unresisting animals (ants and krill) and should be classified as herbivores. Herbivores are of three types.

definitions.name: Grazers
definitions.definition: Animals which devote most of their time to eating are termed grazers. They may be solitary or grouped in herds. Their primary defense is flight, although such action may result in stampedes which could endanger adventurers in their path. When forced to fight, they will fight fiercely until killed or routed.
definitions.examples: antelope; moose; whale (scoops krill from the sea as it swims)

definitions.name: Intermittent
definitions.definition: Herbivores which do not devote full time to eating are termed intermittents. They tend to be solitary. Intermittents usually freeze when an encounter occurs, fleeing if attacked by a larger animal. There is some potential that an intermittent will attack to protect territory or young.

definitions.name: Filters
definitions.definition: Herbivores which pass the environment through their bodies are termed filters. Unlike grazers, which move to food, filters move a flow of water or air through themselves in order to gain food. Generally, filters suck, trip, push, or pull anything (even animals) at close range into a digestive sac. Filters are solitary and generally slow-moving. They will attack reflexively.
definitions.mechanics: Inflicting automatic wounds of 1D per 50 kg or less of animal mass (wound alteration should be ignored for filters). Succeeding against adventurers with a throw of 6+. Prompt struggle by adventurers (at a cost of one endurance point each) will secure an escape on a throw of 7+, DM of +2 for each companion at close range assisting. Throw once per combat round, beginning on the round following the attack. A filter can absorb an animal up to twice its own weight.

definitions.name: Omnivores
definitions.definition: Animals which eat food without regard to its resistance are termed omnivores. The bear, which will eat fruits and berries as readily as it will hunt for animals, is an omnivore. Omnivores are of three types: gatherers, hunters, and eaters.

definitions.name: Gatherers
definitions.definition: Animals which display a greater tendency toward herbivorous behavior are termed gatherers. In most respects, they are similar to intermittents.

definitions.name: Hunters
definitions.definition: Animals which display a greater tendency toward carnivorous behavior are termed hunters. In most respects, they are similar to small or inefficient chasers.

definitions.name: Eaters
definitions.definition: The true omnivore (in the sense that it will eat anything and everything) does not distinguish its food, consuming all that it confronts. Eaters present considerable danger in that they will not avoid adventurers when encountered.
definitions.examples: army ant (when an entire swarm is considered to be one organism)

definitions.name: Carnivores
definitions.definition: Animals which prey on other animals by attacking and killing them in the face of resistance are classed as carnivores. Carnivores are of five basic types: pouncers, chasers, trappers, sirens, and killers.

definitions.name: Pouncers
definitions.definition: Animals which kill their prey by attacking from hiding or by stalking and springing are termed pouncers. Because of the difficulty of coordinating such attacks, pouncers are usually solitary animals. In an encounter, pouncers which have achieved surprise have succeeded in their basic aim and will attack regardless of range. If they do not have surprise, they will sometimes still attack. They will flee if they themselves are surprised.

definitions.name: Chasers
definitions.definition: Animals which kill their prey by attacking after a chase are termed chasers. They tend to be pack animals.

definitions.name: Trappers
definitions.definition: Animals which passively allow their prey to enter a created trap wherein they are killed and then eaten are termed trappers. Trappers tend to be solitary and slow, but will attack any animal which enters their trap. Usually, a trap will not wound or damage a character, but will tend to hold the adventurer to allow the trapper to attempt to kill him.
definitions.mechanics: Generally, any character who is surprised by a trapper at close or short range is then trapped on a throw of 5+. Struggling to escape (in lieu of making any swings or blows, but costing one endurance point) succeeds on a throw of 9+, DM of +1 for each assisting companion. Companions are subject to capture by the trap while providing assistance.

definitions.name: Siren
definitions.definition: Distinct from the trapper, which creates a trap for its prey, a siren also creates a lure to draw prey to the trap. The trap is treated in much the same manner as that of the trapper, but the lure entails additional consideration. In most cases, the lure will be specific to some animal, but will be unnoticed by humans. In rare cases (throw 11+), the lure will be universal, perhaps a smell or scent, or a mirage or beautiful configuration, which will attract characters into a vulnerable position. Very rarely, the lure will be psionic in nature.
definitions.examples: angler fish (its mouth is the trap); venus fly trap

definitions.name: Killers
definitions.definition: Certain carnivores devote much attention to killing, apparently for the act itself, in a kind of blood lust. Killer's reason (such as territorial defense) is replaced by a raw killing instinct. Attacks by killers are fierce and violent. Killers will generally disregard the defender's size as a factor.

definitions.name: Scavengers
definitions.definition: Animals which share or steal the prey of others, or that take the remains of kills, are classed as scavengers. Scavengers are of four types: intimidators, hijackers, carrion-eaters, and reducers.

definitions.name: Intimidators
definitions.definition: Scavengers which establish their claim to food by frightening or threatening other animals are termed intimidators. Their standard procedure is to approach a kill and force other animals away by appearing to be a threat.

definitions.name: Hijackers
definitions.definition: Scavengers which establish their claim to food by simply taking it are termed hijackers. They rely on their superior strength or size to allow them to hijack food because the other animals present cannot effectively object.

definitions.name: Carrion-Eaters
definitions.definition: Scavengers which take dead meat when it becomes available (often waiting patiently for all other threats to disperse before beginning) are termed carrion-eaters.

definitions.name: Reducers
definitions.definition: Scavengers which act constantly on all available food are termed reducers. They eat the remains of food after all other scavengers are finished with it, consuming bone and other leavings.

bookEvents.name: Ravines and Precipices
bookEvents.summary: The party has encountered unexpected geographic features which will retard progress by one day if travel is overland.
bookEvents.mechanics: On foot at close range: lead member will probably fall (throw dexterity or greater to fall; DMs allowed based on appropriate skills), receiving 1D to 6D in wounds. In a land vehicle at close or short range: vehicle will topple (throw 8+ to fall; DMs allowed for ATV or vehicle skill, and DM −1 per 10 kph of speed), inflicting 0D to 5D wounds to each person in the vehicle.
bookEvents.rangeConditions: Fall check: close range (foot). Vehicle topple: close or short range.

bookEvents.name: Seismic Quake
bookEvents.mechanics: Each adventurer must throw strength or less to avoid being thrown to the ground and taking 2D hits (saving throw: dexterity or less).

bookEvents.name: Meteor Shower
bookEvents.summary: Possible only on airless worlds or in asteroid belts, the meteor shower can puncture vacc suits or vehicles.
bookEvents.mechanics: Throw 2D to determine the size and strength of the shower. The result indicates the number of adventurers hit; each one hit must throw the number or less to avoid a vacc suit puncture. If the number is 7+, the shower will puncture a vehicle on a roll of the number or greater. If it does, those inside must roll for injuries.
bookEvents.restrictions: Airless worlds or asteroid belts only.

bookEvents.name: Chameleon
bookEvents.summary: These animals make use of camouflage very effectively.
bookEvents.mechanics: Throw to determine the animal's category and type, as well as other data, but the encounter will be at close range. Once the encounter occurs, throw to determine the animal's reaction and whether it attacks or flees.
bookEvents.rangeConditions: Encounter is always at close range.

bookEvents.name: Psionic Assaulters
bookEvents.summary: Telepathic carnivores (1D in quantity) will initiate an automatic attack on the party of adventurers.
bookEvents.mechanics: All persons not psionically shielded are immediately rendered unconscious and will receive 2D+6 hits. Psionically shielded individuals undergo combat as indicated in the psionics rules. Psionic assaulters always achieve surprise.

bookEvents.name: Storm
bookEvents.summary: A violent rainstorm occurs abruptly, forcing the band to stop and seek shelter, or to continue the journey with increased danger.
bookEvents.mechanics: No additional numeric throws are given in Book 3 for Storm beyond the narrative effect above (stop and seek shelter, or continue with increased danger). Referee adjudicates increased danger.

bookEvents.name: Howling Carnivores (example)
bookEvents.summary: From the Typical Animal Encounter Table (CLEAR Terrain, Regina): out of sight, animals (die roll 11 on that table — Chasers) are heard howling continuously.
bookEvents.mechanics: If the party spends the night nearby, they may attack (roll 7+).

customEvents.name: Dust Storm
customEvents.summary: A wall of grit and wind reduces visibility and travel.
customEvents.mechanics: Overland travel is retarded by one day unless shelter is found. If the party continues, throw 8+ each hour to avoid 1D wounds from debris (DM +1 if wearing a filter mask or vacc suit).

customEvents.name: Flash Flood
customEvents.summary: A sudden rush of water fills the watercourse.
customEvents.mechanics: Throw dexterity or greater to keep footing; failure inflicts 1D wounds and delays the party half a day. Vehicles throw 8+ to be swept (DM for ATV skill, DM −1 per 10 kph).

customEvents.name: Rogue Wave
customEvents.summary: A heavy swell or tidal surge strikes the shore or surface.
customEvents.mechanics: On foot at the water’s edge, throw strength or less to keep footing or take 1D wounds. Small craft throw 8+ to capsize.

customEvents.name: Industrial Wreckage
customEvents.summary: Collapsed works and rusted machinery block the way through old city ground.
customEvents.mechanics: Progress is retarded by one day unless the party detours. At close range, throw dexterity or greater to avoid 1D wounds from unstable debris.

customEvents.name: Howling Carnivores
customEvents.summary: Out of sight, animals are heard howling continuously.
customEvents.mechanics: If the party spends the night nearby, they may attack (roll 7+). Prefer linking this event to a carnivore row on the same table when one exists.

customEvents.name: Volcanic Vent
customEvents.summary: A fumarole or lava crack vents heat and toxic air.
customEvents.mechanics: Throw endurance or less to avoid 1D wounds from fumes. Tainted atmospheres apply DM −2. Vacc or filter gear grants DM +2.

customEvents.name: Local Hazard
customEvents.summary: An unexpected local danger delays the party.
customEvents.mechanics: The referee describes a hazard appropriate to this terrain. Progress is retarded by one day unless the party accepts increased danger (throw 8+ to avoid 1D wounds).
